knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Leading Entries of a Matrix

question.:question/problem:
What is the sum of the leading entries of the $1\text{st},$ $3\text{rd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows in the matrix $A,$ given below?

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-5 & -1 & 8 & -2 \\ 0 & 9 & 1 & 1 \\ 8 & -4 & -4 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -3\end{bmatrix}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The first non-zero entry of each row (from left to right) is the leading entry. 

Therefore, the leading entries of the $1\text{st},$ $3\text{rd},$ and $4\text{th}$ rows of $A$ are $-5,$ $8,$ and $1$, respectively.

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}-5 & -1 & 8 & -2 \\ 0 & 9 & 1 & 1 \\ 8 & -4 & -4 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -3\end{bmatrix}
$$

So, the answer is $-5+8+1=4.$
